activities.description: Medical ID, emergency calling, satellite features, crash detection, and location sharing are worth knowing before you need them.
steps: Open your phone’s emergency and safety settings.
Read what each enabled feature does and how it triggers.
Update only information you are comfortable storing there.

activities.title: Learn a magic square
activities.hook: Understand how a simple number square works and make one yourself.
activities.description: It is a tiny math puzzle that feels more like a trick than homework.
steps: Look up a basic 3×3 magic square.
Verify the row, column, and diagonal sums.
Recreate it from memory or try to derive the pattern.

activities.title: Learn one bird call by ear
activities.hook: Pick a common local bird and learn the sound before the appearance.
activities.description: Recognizing one call can make walks feel surprisingly different because you start noticing the bird before you see it.
steps: Choose one common bird in your area.
Listen to several recordings of its most typical call.
Go outside and spend ten minutes listening for it.

activities.title: Learn how one package is recycled
activities.hook: Pick a confusing package and trace what your local system actually accepts.
activities.description: Rules vary by city, which is why the symbol on the package often does not tell the whole story.
steps: Choose one package you are unsure about.
Check your local recycling authority’s rules.
Learn whether to recycle, trash, drop off, or separate its parts.

activities.title: Learn one car dashboard symbol
activities.hook: Pick a warning light you have seen but never fully understood.
activities.description: Knowing the difference between “check soon” and “stop driving” is useful long before the light actually appears.
steps: Choose one dashboard symbol from your car’s manual or a reputable source.
Learn what it means and how urgent it is.
Find where it appears on your own dashboard if possible.

activities.title: Learn the hidden rule of one board game
activities.hook: Pick a strategy concept that experienced players know but beginners miss.
activities.description: Instead of learning a new game, learn one layer deeper into something you already play.
steps: Choose a game you know the rules to already.
Search for one beginner strategy principle, not a full optimal guide.
Play one round while focusing only on that principle.

activities.title: Do a five-minute doodle duel
activities.hook: Two people get the same random prompt and five minutes to draw it.
activities.description: Bad drawings make this better. The only real rule is that neither person gets extra time.
steps: Generate one random noun or weird prompt.
Set a five-minute timer and draw separately.
Reveal at the same time and invent one award for each drawing.

activities.title: Play the floor-is-lava route
activities.hook: Cross one room without stepping on the normal walking path.
activities.description: Use only safe, sturdy surfaces and make the route just difficult enough to be ridiculous.
steps: Clear breakable or slippery things first.
Choose a start and finish point.
Cross using only safe allowed zones, then try one harder route.

activities.title: Make a one-minute game
activities.hook: Invent a game whose entire rules explanation fits in one minute.
activities.description: Use whatever is already around you: coins, paper, cups, socks, cards, or a phone timer.
steps: Pick one object or room feature as the core mechanic.
Write three rules max.
Play three rounds and change only one rule if it is broken.

activities.title: Do a backwards trivia round
activities.hook: Start with an answer and make everyone invent the question.
activities.description: The funniest question wins, even if it would never appear on real trivia night.
steps: One person secretly chooses an ordinary answer.
Everyone else writes a possible trivia question that leads to it.
Reveal and vote for funniest and most believable.

activities.title: Play screenshot detective
activities.hook: Zoom into random screenshots or photos and guess what they came from.
activities.description: Crop aggressively enough that familiar images become tiny mysteries.
steps: Pick ten safe photos or screenshots with no private information.
Crop each to a confusing detail.
Take turns guessing the original image.

activities.title: Build the tallest paper tower
activities.hook: Use only paper and a small amount of tape if you want.
activities.description: Height matters, but the tower has to stand by itself for ten seconds.
steps: Give everyone the same amount of paper and tape.
Set a 12-minute build timer.
Measure only towers that stand unsupported for ten seconds.

activities.title: Do a two-minute scavenger sprint
activities.hook: Name one category and find as many matching objects as possible before time runs out.
activities.description: Examples: things with circles, objects older than you, or items that start with S.
steps: Pick a category that exists around you.
Set a two-minute timer.
Bring back or photograph as many matching items as you can.

activities.title: Make a household obstacle race
activities.hook: Create a tiny precision course rather than a dangerous speed course.
activities.description: Think sock toss, cup stack, spoon carry, paper-ball target — low stakes and oddly competitive.
steps: Choose four safe mini-challenges.
Put them in a fixed order.
Time each person once and allow one rematch.

activities.title: Play one-word movie pitches
activities.hook: Pitch a movie using only one word at a time, alternating with another person.
activities.description: You have to build the premise together without knowing where the sentence is going.
steps: Choose a genre.
Alternate saying exactly one word at a time.
Stop after 30 words and summarize the accidental movie you invented.

activities.title: Do a map-pin challenge
activities.hook: Drop a random pin on a map and guess what is there before zooming in.
activities.description: Make points for getting the country, terrain, or nearby city right.
steps: Open a map and zoom out.
Drop a pin without studying the label.
Guess three things about the location, then zoom in and score yourself.

activities.title: Play the category alphabet
activities.hook: Pick a category and race through A to Z without getting stuck.
activities.description: Cities, foods, bands, movies, animals, brands — choose something broad enough to be possible.
steps: Choose one category.
Take turns naming an item for each letter in order.
Allow one skip per person and see how far you get.

activities.title: Do a blindfold texture guess
activities.hook: Identify safe household objects using touch alone.
activities.description: Keep everything clean, harmless, and recognizable enough that the guesses are actually possible.
steps: One person chooses five safe objects with distinct textures.
The other closes their eyes or uses a loose blindfold.
Guess each object using only touch, then switch roles.

activities.title: Make a tiny golf course
activities.hook: Turn cups into holes and a rolled-up sock or paper ball into the ball.
activities.description: Build three ridiculous holes around furniture without moving anything heavy.
steps: Choose a soft ball and safe improvised club or use your hand.
Set up three “holes” using cups or targets.
Play one round and add a silly obstacle to the hardest hole.

activities.title: Play six degrees with songs
activities.hook: Connect two completely different artists through collaborations, samples, producers, or features.
activities.description: The stranger the starting pair, the better the chain.
steps: Choose two artists who seem unrelated.
Build a chain using real musical connections.
Verify every link before celebrating the path.

activities.title: Invent a fake sport commentary
activities.hook: Put a mundane task on screen and narrate it like a championship event.
activities.description: Laundry folding, making toast, parking, or a pet walking across the room all become dramatic with the right announcer voice.
steps: Choose one ordinary activity happening nearby.
One person does the task while another commentates dramatically.
Switch roles for a second event.

activities.title: Do a 20-question object hunt
activities.hook: Hide one ordinary object and let someone find it using yes-or-no questions.
activities.description: It is part 20 Questions, part scavenger hunt, and works in almost any room.
steps: One person hides a small safe object in a fair location.
The seeker asks up to 20 yes-or-no questions.
If they fail, give one hot-or-cold hint and finish the hunt.

activities.title: Build a domino chain from random stuff
activities.hook: Make a chain reaction without needing actual dominoes.
activities.description: Books, cards, blocks, boxes, cups, and other safe objects can all become part of the sequence.
steps: Gather lightweight objects that will not break.
Build a short chain with at least one change in height or direction.
Film one final attempt, successful or not.

activities.title: Play “closest wins”
activities.hook: Ask estimation questions where nobody is expected to know the exact answer.
activities.description: How tall is that building? How many songs fit in an hour? How far away is the moon? Closest guess gets the point.
steps: Take turns asking estimation questions.
Everyone locks in a guess before looking anything up.
Check the answer and give one point to the closest guess.

activities.title: Try a single-credit arcade rule
activities.hook: Give yourself one imaginary arcade credit in a game you own.
activities.description: One run, one life, one attempt — when it ends, you are done. The limit makes an old game feel different.
steps: Choose a game with clear runs, rounds, or lives.
Set a one-attempt rule before starting.
When the run ends, save the score and quit instead of restarting.

activities.title: Make a photo bingo card
activities.hook: Create nine tiny visual prompts and try to fill the grid.
activities.description: Use prompts like something crooked, a tiny animal, a perfect circle, or accidental symmetry.
steps: Write nine visual prompts in a 3×3 grid.
Go for a walk and photograph one image per square.
No using the same object for two squares.

activities.title: Do a speed Lego build
activities.hook: Give yourself ten minutes and one absurd prompt.
activities.description: Use whatever bricks or building toys you have and stop exactly when the timer rings.
steps: Choose a prompt like “tiny hotel” or “vehicle for a frog.”
Set a ten-minute timer.
Photograph the build before taking anything apart.

activities.title: Play fake dictionary
activities.hook: Invent definitions for a real word nobody in the group knows.
activities.description: Mix the true definition with convincing fake ones and see who can bluff best.
steps: Choose an obscure but real word.
One person writes the real definition while everyone else invents one.
Shuffle, read all definitions, and vote for the real one.

activities.title: Do a coin-stack tournament
activities.hook: See who can build the tallest stable stack using the same number of coins.
activities.description: Add one weird constraint each round to keep it from being pure patience.
steps: Give each person the same number of coins.
Build the tallest free-standing stack in two minutes.
Play three rounds, adding one new rule each time.

activities.title: Play the no-repeat story game
activities.hook: Build a story one sentence at a time, but ban one common word each round.
activities.description: The story gets stranger as basic words disappear.
steps: Start a story with one sentence.
Take turns adding one sentence.
Every third turn, ban a common word for the rest of the story.

activities.title: Make a tiny bracket for anything
activities.hook: Choose eight things around you and force them into a tournament.
activities.description: Snacks, apps, songs, chairs, neighborhood stores — the subject barely matters once the arguments start.
steps: Choose eight contenders.
Seed them randomly into a bracket.
Debate each matchup quickly and crown one ridiculous champion.

activities.title: Put your phone across the room for one song
activities.hook: Do absolutely nothing with your phone until the song ends.
activities.description: This is not a detox. It is four minutes of giving your attention one less place to go.
steps: Choose one song you already love.
Put your phone somewhere you cannot reach without standing up.
Listen all the way through without doing another task.

activities.title: Watch the light change
activities.hook: Sit near a window for ten minutes and pay attention to the light instead of filling the time.
activities.description: Clouds, reflections, shadows, and color temperature change more than you notice.
steps: Sit somewhere with natural light or a view outside.
Set a quiet ten-minute timer.
Notice three changes without photographing them.

activities.title: Read five pages, no goal
activities.hook: Open any book and read exactly five pages.
activities.description: There is no requirement to keep going, remember anything, or make progress on the book.
steps: Pick the book that feels easiest to open.
Read five pages without checking how many are left.
Close it after page five unless continuing sounds genuinely good.

activities.title: Make the room quieter
activities.hook: Turn off or remove three small sources of noise.
activities.description: Fans you do not need, autoplay, notifications, a humming device, background TV — lower the room’s noise floor for a while.
steps: Stand still and listen for background noise.
Silence three things you can safely turn off or mute.
Sit in the quieter room for five minutes.

activities.title: Do a warm-towel reset
activities.hook: Use a warm damp towel on your face or hands and do nothing else for a minute.
activities.description: It is tiny, physical, and surprisingly effective when you feel overstimulated or stuck.
steps: Warm a clean towel with comfortably warm water.
Rest it on your face or hands for a minute.
Rinse, dry off, and avoid immediately opening an app.

activities.title: Listen to the quietest song you know
activities.hook: Pick something sparse, soft, and slow enough to change the room.
activities.description: One deliberately quiet track can work better than an entire relaxation playlist.
steps: Choose one very quiet song or instrumental.
Lower the lights if you want.
Listen without scrolling until it ends.

activities.title: Sit on the floor with a pillow
activities.hook: Change where you are without going anywhere.
activities.description: A different posture and viewpoint can make a room feel less stale when you are too tired to do much.
steps: Grab one pillow or cushion.
Sit somewhere on the floor you normally would not.
Stay there for at least eight minutes with no task attached.

activities.title: Make a slow snack
activities.hook: Choose something that takes a few minutes to assemble and eat it without multitasking.
activities.description: Fruit, toast, tea, yogurt, popcorn — the food is just an excuse to slow the pace down.
steps: Choose a simple snack you can make slowly.
Prepare it without watching anything.
Sit down and finish it before picking up another task.

activities.title: Rewatch only the opening scene
activities.hook: Watch the first five to ten minutes of a movie you love, then stop.
activities.description: You get the comfort of something familiar without accidentally committing to two hours.
steps: Pick a movie whose opening you remember fondly.
Watch only through the first scene or sequence.
Stop there and let it be enough.

activities.title: Listen to one side of a record
activities.hook: Treat an album like it has a natural stopping point.
activities.description: If you do not have vinyl, use roughly the first 20 minutes of an album and do not shuffle.
steps: Choose an album that works front to back.
Play the first side or about 20 uninterrupted minutes.
Do not browse for the next thing until it ends.

activities.title: Take a low-light shower
activities.hook: Make the bathroom calmer without turning it into a whole spa routine.
activities.description: Use safe dim lighting, leave the phone outside, and let the shower be the only thing happening.
steps: Set safe low lighting before you start.
Leave your phone out of reach.
Take a normal shower without rushing or adding extra steps.

activities.title: Look through one old photo album
activities.hook: Browse one small chunk of old photos without sorting or editing anything.
activities.description: The rule is no cleanup. Just look at a specific month, trip, or album and let the memories be messy.
steps: Choose one old album, month, or trip.
Scroll slowly for ten minutes.
Favorite one photo only if it really stands out; do not start organizing.

activities.title: Make a tiny reading nook
activities.hook: Move one light, pillow, or chair to make a temporary cozy spot.
activities.description: No room makeover required. Create one place that feels good enough for the next 30 minutes.
steps: Choose one corner or seat.
Adjust only three things: light, softness, and clutter.
Use the spot immediately for reading, music, or doing nothing.

activities.title: Watch one fireplace or aquarium feed
activities.hook: Put on a calm live feed and let it be background rather than content.
activities.description: Choose something visually slow enough that you do not feel like you have to keep watching.
steps: Choose a live aquarium, fireplace, train-window, or similar slow feed.
Put it on a larger screen if convenient.
Do something quiet nearby or simply sit for 15 minutes.

activities.title: Do a no-input tea break
activities.hook: Make a drink and consume no new information while you have it.
activities.description: No news, messages, videos, podcasts, or reading. Just the drink and whatever is already in the room.
steps: Make tea, coffee, cocoa, or another simple drink.
Put devices out of reach.
Finish the drink without consuming any media.

activities.title: Play one ambient track in the dark
activities.hook: Let one long instrumental or ambient track be the entire activity.
activities.description: No playlist management, no browsing, no productivity purpose.
steps: Choose one ambient, classical, or instrumental track.
Dim the room as much as feels comfortable.
Listen until the track ends or 20 minutes pass.

activities.title: Take a blanket outside
activities.hook: Sit outside somewhere comfortable with a blanket for a little while.
activities.description: A porch, yard, balcony, park, or even open car hatch works. The goal is simply a change in air and temperature.
steps: Choose a safe nearby outdoor spot.
Bring one blanket, jacket, or comfortable layer.
Sit for at least 15 minutes without turning it into an errand.

activities.title: Do a five-minute hand massage
activities.hook: Give your hands attention after a day of typing, gripping, or scrolling.
activities.description: Use lotion if you have it and slowly work through palms, fingers, and wrists.
steps: Apply lotion or just warm your hands together.
Massage each palm, finger, and wrist slowly.
Finish by opening and closing your hands ten times.

activities.title: Read something printed
activities.hook: Pick any physical page and get away from glowing rectangles for a bit.
activities.description: Magazine, comic, cookbook, newspaper, manual, zine — it does not need to be serious reading.
steps: Choose one printed thing within reach.
Read for at least ten minutes.
Stop at a natural break instead of checking your phone mid-page.

activities.title: Watch clouds until one changes shape
activities.hook: Give the sky a very small job to do.
activities.description: Find one cloud and watch long enough to see it noticeably stretch, split, fade, or merge.
steps: Find a comfortable place with a view of the sky.
Choose one cloud.
Stay with it until you can clearly describe how it changed.

activities.title: Make the bed extra early
activities.hook: Reset the bed before you are tired enough to care.
activities.description: Fresh sheets if you have energy, or just straighten everything and make the room feel ready for later.
steps: Clear anything that does not belong on the bed.
Straighten or change the bedding.
Add one small comfort for later: water, book, charger, or extra pillow.

activities.title: Take a slow drive with one album
activities.hook: Drive a familiar safe route with a full album and no destination pressure.
activities.description: This is for when sitting still feels bad but doing an activity sounds worse.
steps: Choose a familiar low-stress route and an album.
Set navigation only if needed before moving.
Drive safely, do not handle your phone, and head home when the album or route ends.

activities.title: Do a five-sense reset
activities.hook: Name one thing you can notice with each sense, slowly.
activities.description: It is a tiny grounding exercise without turning the moment into a wellness project.
steps: Notice five things you can see.
Then name four you can feel, three you can hear, two you can smell, and one you can taste.
Stop there — no journaling required.

activities.title: Let one room stay messy
activities.hook: Choose one small area you are officially not fixing tonight.
activities.description: Sometimes the relaxing thing is deciding what does not need attention yet.
steps: Pick one messy area that is not unsafe or urgent.
Move only anything that blocks actual use.
Decide out loud or in a note that it can wait until another day.

activities.title: Listen to a full rainstorm recording
activities.hook: Use one continuous field recording instead of a playlist.
activities.description: The lack of song changes makes it easier for your brain to stop anticipating the next thing.
steps: Find one uninterrupted rain, ocean, train, or forest recording.
Set the volume low enough to fade into the room.
Lie down, read, or simply listen for at least 20 minutes.

activities.title: Send someone a one-song recommendation
activities.hook: Pick one song for one specific person and tell them why in one sentence.
activities.description: No playlist dump. One track feels personal enough to actually listen to.
steps: Think of one person and one song that genuinely fits them.
Send the song with a one-sentence reason.
Do not follow it with five more recommendations.

activities.title: Ask for a photo from today
activities.hook: Text someone you like and ask them to send one completely ordinary photo from their day.
activities.description: It is a small way to see someone’s actual life without forcing a big conversation.
steps: Pick someone you are comfortable texting casually.
Ask for one random photo from their day and send one back.
Let the conversation end there if it wants to.

activities.title: Do a ten-minute voice-note swap
activities.hook: Trade one short voice note about whatever is currently on your mind.
activities.description: It is warmer than texting but less commitment than a full phone call.
steps: Ask one person if they want to trade a voice note.
Keep yours under five minutes.
Listen to theirs without multitasking and reply once.

activities.title: Compare camera rolls from the same day
activities.hook: Pick a date you were both together and see what each person photographed.
activities.description: Two people can remember the exact same day completely differently.
steps: Choose one shared day or trip.
Open both camera rolls to that date.
Take turns showing five photos and telling the tiny story behind each.

activities.title: Trade a tiny favor
activities.hook: Each person picks one five-minute thing that would make their day easier.
activities.description: Charge something, refill water, proofread a text, carry a box, find a link — tiny favors count.
steps: Each person names one favor that truly takes under five minutes.
Do them immediately.
No keeping score or upgrading the favor into a bigger task.

activities.title: Make a two-person snack rating
activities.hook: Choose three snacks and rate them on absurdly specific categories.
activities.description: Crunch confidence, road-trip potential, midnight energy, packaging drama — invent criteria that make no sense.
steps: Choose three snacks you already have or can get easily.
Invent four silly rating categories.
Score each snack and compare the final winner.

activities.title: Walk and swap one story each
activities.hook: Take a short walk where each person tells one story the other has never heard.
activities.description: The story can be tiny — a weird teacher, a childhood habit, an awkward trip, anything specific.
steps: Go on an easy walk with one other person.
Person one tells a story without being interrupted by phones.
Switch before heading home.

activities.title: Plan a $20 imaginary day
activities.hook: Give yourselves a tiny fake budget and design the best possible day nearby.
activities.description: You do not have to actually do the plan. The fun is finding what you could squeeze out of the limit.
steps: Set a total imaginary budget of $20 per person or less.
Find three real local stops or activities that fit.
Choose the version you would genuinely consider doing someday.

activities.title: Swap one app recommendation
activities.hook: Each person gets one app, game, website, or tool to recommend.
activities.description: Explain the exact thing it is good for instead of giving a generic “you should download this.”
steps: Choose one digital thing you actually use.
Show the other person the feature that makes it worth having.
Try their recommendation for five minutes before judging it.

activities.title: Do a porch or stoop hang
activities.hook: Sit outside together somewhere close to home with no destination.
activities.description: Sometimes the activity is just moving the conversation to a different physical place.
steps: Choose a safe porch, stoop, yard, balcony, or nearby bench.
Bring a drink or snack if you want.
Stay until the conversation naturally ends, not until a timer says so.

activities.title: Make a shared photo album for one thing
activities.hook: Create one tiny album around a person, trip, pet, project, or running joke.
activities.description: Keep it narrow enough that you can actually finish the first version today.
steps: Choose one specific theme.
Each person adds up to 15 photos.
Give the album a name and stop before it becomes a giant archive project.

activities.title: Ask someone to teach you their shortcut
activities.hook: Have a friend show you one little thing they do faster or better than you.
activities.description: Cooking, phone settings, folding, game controls, makeup, parking, knots — anything counts.
steps: Ask one person for a tiny skill they can demonstrate in under ten minutes.
Watch once without interrupting.
Try it yourself while they coach only if needed.

activities.title: Do a family object story
activities.hook: Pick one old object in the house and ask someone what they know about it.
activities.description: Furniture, cookware, tools, photos, jewelry, decorations — ordinary objects can carry surprisingly specific stories.
steps: Choose one object that has been around a long time.
Ask an older or knowledgeable family member where it came from.
Write down one detail you would otherwise forget.

activities.title: Make a tiny group poll
activities.hook: Ask one oddly specific question and collect five answers.
activities.description: Examples: best smell in the world, ideal pizza shape, or one app everyone should delete.
steps: Write one question with no serious stakes.
Send it to a small group or ask people in person.
Share the funniest pattern or most unexpected answer.

activities.title: Do an errand together on purpose
activities.hook: Take one boring errand and make it the plan instead of squeezing it between plans.
activities.description: Add a walk, snack, music choice, or tiny detour so the task becomes shared time.
steps: Choose one errand one of you already needs to do.
Go together and let the other person choose the music or route.
Add one small optional stop on the way home.

activities.title: Trade “you would like this” links
activities.hook: Each person finds exactly three links the other person would genuinely enjoy.
activities.description: Articles, products, videos, weird maps, recipes, photos — the goal is specificity, not volume.
steps: Pick one person you know well.
Find three links that match their actual taste.
Trade all three at once and explain your strongest pick.

activities.title: Make a two-person time capsule
activities.hook: Choose five tiny things that capture right now and seal them in a note or folder.
activities.description: Screenshots, a current favorite song, one photo, a receipt, a sentence — future-you does not need a giant box.
steps: Choose five digital or physical items that represent this month.
Add one short note from each person.
Set a date six or twelve months away to reopen it.

activities.title: Take turns choosing one block
activities.hook: Go for a walk where each person controls exactly one block at a time.
activities.description: No arguing about the route. When your block ends, control passes.
steps: Choose who gets the first block.
At each intersection, the current person picks the direction.
After 20 minutes, use the shortest route home.

activities.title: Cook from two favorite ingredients
activities.hook: Each person picks one ingredient they love; make one dish that uses both.
activities.description: The combination might be obvious or weird. Either way, you have a shared constraint.
steps: Each person names one reasonable ingredient.
Choose a dish that can include both.
Cook it together without adding a third “main character” ingredient.

activities.title: Do a one-episode club
activities.hook: Pick one episode of something neither person has seen and treat it like a tiny club.
activities.description: Watch once, then spend five minutes comparing what you liked, hated, or predict next.
steps: Choose a show neither of you is already watching.
Watch only the first episode or one standalone episode.
Afterward, each person gives a one-minute verdict.

activities.title: Make a shared “someday” map
activities.hook: Drop pins for places you would realistically want to try together.
activities.description: Keep it local or regional so the map becomes usable, not a fantasy travel board.
steps: Open a shared map or note.
Each person adds three places within realistic reach.
Choose one pin that could happen in the next month.

activities.title: Swap childhood snacks
activities.hook: Each person picks a snack or drink they strongly associate with being younger.
activities.description: The best part is the story attached to it, not whether the snack is objectively good.
steps: Each person chooses one childhood snack or drink.
Find them if practical or use the closest substitute.
Taste together and explain the memory attached to yours.

activities.title: Make a “this or that” walk
activities.hook: Use every intersection as a conversation prompt.
activities.description: Before choosing the direction, ask a quick either-or question and let the answer decide left or right.
steps: Agree which answer means left and which means right.
At each intersection, ask a new either-or question.
Stop after 20 minutes and navigate home normally.

activities.title: Do a tiny skill trade
activities.hook: Spend 15 minutes teaching each other one thing.
activities.description: Keep both skills small enough that the other person can actually try them immediately.
steps: Each person chooses a skill teachable in 15 minutes.
Person one teaches while person two tries it.
Switch roles exactly halfway through.

activities.title: Plan tomorrow’s breakfast together
activities.hook: Make one tiny future plan that is easy enough to actually happen.
activities.description: Pick the food, time, and place now, then tomorrow starts with something already decided.
steps: Choose breakfast at home or one nearby place.
Agree on a realistic time.
Put it on both calendars or send one confirming text.

activities.title: Make a one-key text shortcut
activities.hook: Turn a phrase you type constantly into a tiny expansion.
activities.description: Email addresses, meeting phrases, links, signatures, or common replies can save more friction than flashy automations.
steps: Pick one phrase you type several times a week.
Create a text replacement or snippet for it.
Test it in two different apps.

activities.title: Audit your menu bar
activities.hook: Remove, reorder, or hide the icons you never actually use.
activities.description: Ten minutes of cleanup can make the top of your screen feel much calmer.
steps: List the menu-bar icons you can see right now.
Hide or remove anything you have not used recently.
Reorder the remaining icons by how often you touch them.

activities.title: Make a local start page
activities.hook: Create one simple HTML file with the links you actually want when a browser opens.
activities.description: No framework, no deploy, no account — just a useful page that lives on your computer.
steps: Create a blank HTML file.
Add your most-used links and one tiny personal touch.
Set it as a browser home page or bookmark it.

activities.title: Set up a throwaway browser profile
activities.hook: Create a clean browser profile for testing, shopping, school, or one specific project.
activities.description: Separating one context can reduce tab chaos without forcing you to reorganize your whole browser.
steps: Choose one context that deserves separation.
Create a new browser profile with only the needed extensions.
Pin or bookmark the few sites that belong there.

activities.title: Make a one-tap clipboard tool
activities.hook: Create a shortcut that copies one frequently needed piece of text.
activities.description: A template, address, link, ID format, or support response can become one quick action.
steps: Choose one piece of non-sensitive text you often hunt for.
Build a shortcut or automation that copies it.
Add it somewhere easy to trigger and test it twice.

activities.title: Find your oldest installed app
activities.hook: Look at the software that has survived the longest on your device.
activities.description: Decide whether it is still useful, nostalgic, abandoned, or somehow immortal.
steps: Open your installed-app list or Applications folder.
Find one of the oldest things you still have.
Open it once, then keep or remove it deliberately.

activities.title: Build a tiny data dashboard
activities.hook: Take one number you care about and display it in the simplest possible way.
activities.description: Storage, weather, steps, GitHub activity, time left in the day — one metric is enough.
steps: Choose one data source you can access safely.
Display only one or two values in a tiny page, script, or widget.
Stop before adding charts unless the chart is actually useful.

activities.title: Make a QR code for your Wi-Fi
activities.hook: Create a scannable code guests can use instead of asking for the password.
activities.description: Keep the code somewhere private enough for your situation, like a printed card inside the house.
steps: Use a trusted local or offline QR method if possible.
Encode your guest Wi-Fi details, not a network you do not want shared.
Test with another device before printing or saving it.

activities.title: Try one macOS accessibility feature
activities.hook: Explore an accessibility setting as a power-user feature, not only as an accommodation.
activities.description: Hover Text, Reduce Motion, Voice Control, background sounds, zoom, or pointer options may solve a surprisingly specific annoyance.
steps: Open Accessibility settings.
Pick one feature you have never tried.
Use it for ten minutes, then keep it only if it improves something.

activities.title: Make a smart screenshot folder
activities.hook: Automate screenshots into a folder or naming pattern that stops them taking over your desktop.
activities.description: One small rule can keep a constant source of digital clutter under control.
steps: Choose where screenshots should live.
Configure your system or automation to save or move them there.
Take three test screenshots and verify the workflow.

activities.title: Benchmark one annoying task
activities.hook: Time how long a repetitive digital task actually takes, then improve it once.
activities.description: You only need one before-and-after measurement to know whether an automation is worth keeping.
steps: Choose a digital task you repeat often.
Time yourself doing it normally once.
Change one thing — shortcut, template, automation — and time it again.

activities.title: Build a tiny status page for yourself
activities.hook: Make one page that says whether your own important stuff is working.
activities.description: It can be as simple as links plus green/red checks for a website, server, or project you care about.
steps: Choose two or three things worth checking.
Build the smallest page or script that checks or links to each one.
Keep it local unless you truly need it online.

activities.title: Clean one cloud folder
activities.hook: Pick a single cloud-storage folder and make its purpose obvious.
activities.description: Do not organize the whole drive. Rename, delete, and group only what is inside one folder.
steps: Choose one cloud folder you open often.
Delete obvious junk and rename unclear files.
Create at most two subfolders if they genuinely help.

activities.title: Make a terminal alias you will remember
activities.hook: Turn one command you type often into a short alias with a name that makes sense to you.
activities.description: The best alias is boring and obvious enough that you still remember it next month.
steps: Pick one safe command you use repeatedly.
Add a clearly named alias to your shell config.
Reload the shell and test it in a harmless directory.

activities.title: Inspect what launches at login
activities.hook: See what your computer is starting before you even ask it to.
activities.description: Remove only things you recognize and do not want running automatically.
steps: Open login-item or startup settings.
Identify every item before changing anything.
Disable only apps you know you do not need at login.

activities.title: Make a tiny API request by hand
activities.hook: Use curl or a simple client to ask one public API for one piece of data.
activities.description: Weather, random facts, public JSON, or a test endpoint is enough to make the request-response cycle concrete.
steps: Choose a safe public API or test endpoint that needs no secret key.
Send one GET request and inspect the raw response.
Extract one field manually or with a simple tool.

activities.title: Turn a webpage into an app shortcut
activities.hook: Save one web tool you use constantly as a standalone web app or dock shortcut.
activities.description: It is a tiny change, but separating one site from browser tabs can make it feel much more intentional.
steps: Choose one site you use almost like an app.
Use your browser’s add-to-dock or install-web-app feature if available.
Open it once and confirm links behave the way you expect.

activities.title: Map your home network
activities.hook: Identify the devices currently connected to your own network.
activities.description: The goal is awareness, not hacking. Name the devices you recognize and investigate only your own equipment.
steps: Open your router or trusted network-management app.
Count and identify devices you own or expect.
Rename unclear devices in the router interface if supported and safe.

activities.title: Make a one-screen settings cheat sheet
activities.hook: Write down the five settings you always forget where to find.
activities.description: It can be a note with paths like “Settings → Accessibility → …” instead of another app or automation.
steps: Think of five settings you have searched for more than once.
Write the exact navigation path for each.
Pin the note somewhere easy to retrieve.

activities.title: Try a different DNS resolver
activities.hook: Learn what DNS does and test a reputable alternative on one device.
activities.description: This is a small networking experiment, not a promise that everything will become magically faster.
steps: Read a short explanation of DNS first.
Choose a reputable resolver and note your current settings before changing anything.
Test browsing, then revert if you notice problems.

activities.title: Make a tiny local web server
activities.hook: Serve one folder from your computer and open it in the browser.
activities.description: A local server turns “files in a folder” into a real web environment with almost no setup.
steps: Choose a folder containing a simple HTML file.
Start a local server with a tool already installed or a safe built-in option.
Open localhost in your browser, then stop the server when finished.

activities.title: Create a clean demo account
activities.hook: Make a separate non-sensitive sample profile for testing your own app or website.
activities.description: A realistic demo state is useful for screenshots, testing, and showing work without exposing personal data.
steps: Choose one project that benefits from a demo state.
Create fake but realistic sample data with no real personal information.
Save the credentials securely if you need to reuse them.

activities.title: Check your battery’s actual health
activities.hook: Look at the battery-health information your device already exposes.
activities.description: Learn capacity, cycle count, or charging settings without installing sketchy cleanup software.
steps: Open your device’s built-in battery information.
Find health, capacity, or cycle-count data if available.
Read what your manufacturer considers normal before drawing conclusions.

activities.title: Make a “send later” workflow
activities.hook: Set up one reliable way to write something now and have it go out later.
activities.description: Email scheduling, reminders, or delayed shortcuts can stop tiny follow-ups from living in your head.
steps: Choose one app you already use that supports scheduling or reminders.
Create a harmless test message or reminder for ten minutes from now.
Confirm it behaves as expected before relying on it.

activities.title: Reduce one app to essentials
activities.hook: Turn off every nonessential notification, badge, or permission in one noisy app.
activities.description: Do not overhaul your whole phone. Make one app earn the attention it is asking for.
steps: Choose one app that interrupts you too often.
Review its notification categories and permissions.
Keep only the alerts or access that serve a clear purpose.

activities.title: Refill the things you always run out of
activities.hook: Pick three boring consumables and top them up now.
activities.description: Soap, paper, charger batteries, pet supplies, coffee, printer paper — tiny restocks prevent annoying future interruptions.
steps: Choose three items you use constantly.
Refill or move backup stock where it belongs.
Add only truly low items to your shopping list.

activities.title: Fix one bad contact card
activities.hook: Clean up one person in your contacts instead of the whole address book.
activities.description: Add the right name, photo, company, birthday, or duplicate merge — just enough that future-you benefits.
steps: Pick one contact you message often.
Correct one missing or messy detail.
Merge duplicates if you are certain they are the same person.

activities.title: Make a spare charging spot
activities.hook: Use a cable and adapter you already own to create one dependable place to charge.
activities.description: A charger where you actually need it is more useful than three tangled in a drawer.
steps: Pick a place where you often need power.
Find a safe spare cable and adapter.
Route it neatly enough that it can stay there.

activities.title: Clear five browser tabs properly
activities.hook: Close five tabs by deciding what each one needs, not by rage-quitting the window.
activities.description: Save, act, bookmark, copy the useful bit, or close — each tab gets a real decision.
steps: Choose the five oldest or least useful tabs.
For each, decide: do, save, or close.
Stop after five even if 80 tabs remain.

activities.title: Update one emergency contact
activities.hook: Make sure one person or piece of emergency info on your phone is current.
activities.description: It takes minutes and matters more than most settings cleanup.
steps: Open your phone’s emergency or medical information.
Check one contact or critical detail.
Update it only if needed and you are comfortable storing it.

activities.title: Make a “leaving home” basket
activities.hook: Give keys, wallet, earbuds, badges, and other exit items one obvious landing zone.
activities.description: Use any bowl, tray, hook, or box you already have before buying an organizer.
steps: List the items you regularly search for before leaving.
Choose one spot near your normal exit.
Put the items there and remove unrelated clutter from that spot.

activities.title: Check one subscription renewal
activities.hook: Find one recurring charge and confirm the price, renewal date, and whether you still want it.
activities.description: One subscription is manageable; a full financial audit is not required.
steps: Pick one subscription you are unsure about.
Check its current price and next renewal date in the official app or receipt.
Keep, cancel, or set a reminder before renewal.

activities.title: Make a simple lost-item label
activities.hook: Add contact info to one thing you would hate to lose.
activities.description: A luggage tag, device lock-screen note, key tag, or small card can make an accidental loss easier to recover.
steps: Choose one high-value or frequently carried item.
Add a safe contact method without oversharing personal information.
Check that the label is readable and secure.

activities.title: Measure one awkward space
activities.hook: Get the dimensions of the place you keep guessing about.
activities.description: A shelf, drawer, wall, closet opening, car trunk, or desk gap becomes much easier to shop or plan for once measured.
steps: Pick one space you may buy or build something for.
Measure width, height, and depth.
Save the dimensions in a note with a photo.

activities.title: Create a “use first” food zone
activities.hook: Put soon-to-expire food in one visible part of the fridge or pantry.
activities.description: You do not need to inventory everything. Just make the items with a deadline harder to forget.
steps: Scan for food that should be used soon.
Choose one visible shelf, bin, or section.
Move those items together and plan one meal or snack around them.

activities.title: Reset one pair of headphones
activities.hook: Clean, charge, update, and reconnect the headphones you use most.
activities.description: A ten-minute maintenance pass can fix a lot of tiny daily annoyances at once.
steps: Wipe the headphones safely according to manufacturer guidance.
Charge them and check for updates if applicable.
Reconnect and test both audio and microphone.

activities.title: Make a tiny home inventory
activities.hook: Photograph five important or expensive items and save the basics.
activities.description: A small start is more useful than waiting to document everything someday.
steps: Choose five items worth documenting.
Photograph each plus model or serial information when appropriate.
Store the photos in a clearly named private album or folder.

activities.title: Fix one squeak
